relations.note: Translated from the printed Hebrew Bibles of 1604-1611, every one of them a Masoretic text; BHSA is the Masoretic Text as the Leningrad Codex preserves it.
relations.source: The Translators to the Reader (1611); Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible, 3rd ed. (2012)

relations.note: The translators published no Greek of their own; Scrivener reconstructed it reading by reading from the editions of Erasmus, Stephanus and Beza they followed.
relations.source: F. H. A. Scrivener, The New Testament in the Original Greek according to the Text followed in the Authorised Version (1881)

relations.note: The translators revised the Bishops' Bible and were to use Tyndale's, among other English versions, where it agreed better with the original.
relations.source: The rules given to the translators (1604), rule 14

relations.note: The translators revised the Bishops' Bible and were to use the Geneva, among other English versions, where it agreed better with the original.
relations.source: The rules given to the translators (1604), rule 14

relations.note: Both are the Received Text. Scrivener chose at each place among the readings of Erasmus, Stephanus and Beza the one the Authorised Version followed.
relations.source: F. H. A. Scrivener, The New Testament in the Original Greek according to the Text followed in the Authorised Version (1881)

relations.note: Tyndale translated from Erasmus's Greek, from which the Received Text descends.
relations.source: The readings it prints: Acts 8:37, Matthew 17:21, John 5:4, 1 John 5:7 and the doxology of the Lord's Prayer

relations.note: The American recension of the Revised Version of 1881-1885, which revised the Authorised Version against the manuscripts found since.
relations.source: Title page of the American Standard Version (1901): "being the version set forth A.D. 1611, compared with the most ancient authorities and revised"

relations.note: An update of the American Standard Version of 1901.
relations.source: Preface to the World English Bible

relations.note: The New Testament was conformed in places to the Byzantine Majority Text of Robinson and Pierpont and of Hodges and Farstad; the edition of Robinson and Pierpont held here is the later one of 2018.
relations.source: Preface to the World English Bible

relations.note: An open-licensed update of the American Standard Version of 1901.
relations.source: unfoldingWord Literal Text, manifest of release 90 (2026)

relations.note: Brenton translated the Vatican text in Valpy's reprint of the Sixtine edition of 1587, the Greek printed facing his English.
relations.source: L. C. L. Brenton, preface to The Septuagint Version of the Old Testament (1844)

relations.note: For the Apocrypha added in 1851 Brenton adapted the Authorised Version rather than translating afresh; 3 and 4 Maccabees, which it lacks, were translated for that edition.
relations.source: Preface to Brenton's edition with the Apocrypha (Samuel Bagster and Sons, 1851)

relations.note: The Sixtine edition follows Codex Vaticanus and fills its gaps from other manuscripts; Swete prints the codex as it stands.
relations.source: H. B. Swete, An Introduction to the Old Testament in Greek (1900)

relations.note: Translated from the Latin Vulgate; Challoner's revision follows the Clementine text.
relations.source: Title page of the Douay-Rheims Bible, American edition of 1899: "translated from the Latin Vulgate"

relations.note: The Ge'ez Old Testament was translated from the Greek Septuagint between the fourth and the sixth century.
relations.source: Michael A. Knibb, Translating the Bible: The Ethiopic Version of the Old Testament (1999)

relations.note: The Synod approved translating the Old Testament from the Masoretic Text in 1862; where the Septuagint has words the Hebrew does not, the edition prints them in square brackets.
relations.source: I. A. Chistovich, История перевода Библии на русский язык (1899)

relations.note: Translated from the Masoretic Text.
relations.source: Title page: The Holy Scriptures according to the Masoretic Text (Jewish Publication Society, 1917)

relations.note: Luther translated the Old Testament from the printed Hebrew of his day, a Masoretic text.
relations.source: Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible, 3rd ed. (2012)

relations.note: Luther translated from Erasmus's Greek, from which the Received Text descends, and the 1912 revision keeps its readings.
relations.source: The readings it prints: Acts 8:37, Matthew 17:21 and 18:11, Luke 17:36, John 5:4 and the doxology of the Lord's Prayer

relations.note: Its Greek is the Received Text throughout.
relations.source: The readings it prints: 1 John 5:7, Acts 8:37, Matthew 17:21 and 18:11, Luke 17:36, John 5:4 and the doxology of the Lord's Prayer

relations.note: Young's Greek is the Received Text.
relations.source: The readings it prints: Acts 8:37, Matthew 17:21, John 5:4 and 1 John 5:7

relations.note: Almeida translated the New Testament from the Greek of the Received Text.
relations.source: The readings it prints: 1 John 5:7, Acts 8:37 and the doxology of the Lord's Prayer

relations.note: Translated from the printed Hebrew of its day, a Masoretic text.
relations.source: Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible, 3rd ed. (2012)

relations.note: Segond translated the Old Testament from the Hebrew, a Masoretic text, and numbers it as the Hebrew does.
relations.source: Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible, 3rd ed. (2012)

relations.note: Ohienko translated the Old Testament from the Hebrew, a Masoretic text.
relations.source: Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible, 3rd ed. (2012)

relations.note: Hooke's committee translated the Old Testament from the Hebrew, a Masoretic text.
relations.source: Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible, 3rd ed. (2012)

relations.note: Nestle printed at each place the reading on which two of his three editions agreed: Tischendorf's eighth, Westcott and Hort, and Weymouth, replaced by Weiss from 1901.
relations.source: Eberhard Nestle, preface to Novum Testamentum Graece (1898)

relations.note: Nestle printed at each place the reading on which two of his three editions agreed: Tischendorf's eighth, Westcott and Hort, and Weymouth, replaced by Weiss from 1901.
relations.source: Eberhard Nestle, preface to Novum Testamentum Graece (1898)

relations.note: Its New Testament was made from the Greek behind the Revised Version of 1881, which is the Greek the American Standard Version renders.
relations.source: Jost Oliver Zetzsche, The Bible in China: The History of the Union Version (1999)
